verdict.rationale: First-party marketing describes a built-in 'Payroll AI' that collects time and attendance data, spots inconsistencies, and texts the admin, so a narrow set of payroll prep tasks is handed to an in-product AI. That is the product's own AI capability, but it is a single marketing line, and nothing shows a user can assign arbitrary tasks to it. Auto-payroll scheduling and human experts are rule-based automation and services, not an AI assistant, so they earn no credit. Missing for 10: evidence of a conversational or general-purpose assistant users can direct, documentation of what tasks can be delegated and how, an approval/oversight flow for AI actions, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
